propositions: Nested pytest child process hangs during session cleanup after test execution completes, consuming the 90-second timeout budget through recursive deletion of unrelated shared numbered temp directories.

Pytest session finish synchronously scans and deletes stale numbered temp trees in the user-global root; with 400,000+ entries this cleanup cost scales from 0.88s (private basetemp) to 10.8s (shared root).
The nested pytest invocation omits --basetemp argument despite caller owning tmp_path, causing child to join user-global numbered temp root instead of isolated directory.
Private caller-owned basetemp passed via --basetemp isolates pytest session-finish cleanup without changing test selection, environment, timeout, capture, or ambient-store assertions.

Regression test confirms fix: pre-existing sentinel in another run's temp tree is deleted by nested pytest without fix, preserved after fix, and returns to deleted state under exact omitted-basetemp mutation.
